name: Ptosis surgery for asymmetry

card.summary: Eyelid-lifting surgery to correct a drooping upper lid so the eyes match; an established procedure, with uneven lids a recognised complication.
card.note: Evidence covers ptosis repair generally; asymmetry results can recur or be uneven after surgery.

quick.overview:
Ptosis is a drooping upper eyelid. Surgery tightens or replaces the lifting mechanism, and in looksmaxxing discussions it is cited as a way to make a droopy lid match the other eye.

Surgical series describe it as an established treatment for mild to severe ptosis, but outcomes vary by cause and technique.
quick.mechanism: Techniques include shortening the levator muscle, resecting Muller's muscle, or suspending the lid from the forehead muscle (frontalis sling) when the lid muscle is very weak.
quick.risks: Reported complications include uneven lids after surgery, dry eye if the eye does not close fully, bleeding, infection, rarely loss of lid movement, and recurrence.

lead: Ptosis surgery lifts a drooping upper eyelid so the eye opens fully and matches its partner. When one lid sits lower than the other, the face reads as uneven and the eye can look smaller or sleepy; repairing the lid is how people with noticeable lid asymmetry aim for a more symmetrical, more open and alert eye area. [1][3]

Ptosis is drooping of the upper eyelid, caused by dysfunction of the levator muscle, its nerve supply, or the sympathetic supply to Muller's muscle, with causes including aging, congenital factors, trauma and conditions such as myasthenia gravis. [1] Surgical options include levator resection or advancement, Muller's muscle resection and frontalis or Whitnall slings. [1][4]

Plastic-surgery reviews describe repair as both a functional and a cosmetic problem, with growing patient demand for an optimal cosmetic result. [5] Brow position is evaluated alongside the lids, because brow shape influences upper lid fold height and crease curvature. [6]
infobox: Levator resection, Muller's muscle resection, frontalis sling, Whitnall sling [1]
0.1% oxymetazoline drops, FDA-approved 2020 for acquired ptosis [1]

paras: Ptosis is classified as neurogenic, myogenic, aponeurotic, mechanical or neurotoxic; pseudoptosis describes apparent drooping caused by poor lid support or a higher lid on the opposite side.[1]

Levator resection is generally used when levator function is 5 mm or less, and Muller's muscle resection is another option. A frontalis sling is described as preferred in oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy and considered most effective for moderate to severe congenital ptosis, while a Whitnall sling is often chosen when cosmetic appearance is the priority.[1] Children are usually not operated on until about age 4 or 5.[1]
A 2019 series described minimally invasive conjoint fascial sheath suspension for mild to moderate unilateral or bilateral blepharoptosis, intended to shorten recovery and avoid conspicuous scars.[2]

A 2021 review describes posterior Muller muscle-conjunctival resection as a choice for mild to moderate ptosis with good levator function, noting predictable cosmetic outcomes and a lower reoperation rate, while external levator resection is preferred with lesser levator function or ocular surface disease. [4] A randomized trial compared external levator advancement with Muller muscle-conjunctival resection in mild to moderate aponeurotic ptosis with good levator function. [7] A 2018 review notes that innovations over recent years have focused on refining established methods and treating more severe conditions. [8]

Complications include uneven eyelids after surgery, dry eyes if closure is incomplete, bleeding and infection, and rarely loss of lid movement. In one study cited on Wikipedia, half of patients needed further surgery within 8 to 10 years.[1]

A randomized clinical trial of 2018 compared external levator advancement with Muller muscle-conjunctival resection for aponeurotic ptosis, with eyelid height (marginal reflex distance) at one month as the primary outcome. [7] A 2022 systematic review of pediatric repair covered 23 studies and 730 patients, mostly case series, and reported reoperation rates averaging about 17 percent for external levator resection and 22 percent for internal approaches, with commonest complications not sight-threatening. [9] A 2018 systematic review of frontalis-orbicularis muscle advancement found 38 articles, many case series with varied techniques. [10] A 2019 series described conjoint fascial sheath suspension for mild to moderate blepharoptosis. [2] No studies found on ptosis surgery framed specifically as looksmaxxing asymmetry correction.

timeline.event: FDA approves 0.1% oxymetazoline eye drops for acquired ptosis.[1]

Droopy upper lid rises to the same level as the other
Eyes look more equal and more open
angle.text: Ptosis repair raises a lower-set upper eyelid so the two eyes line up, which reads as a more symmetrical and alert face.
